leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eight members explicitly prefer a single-achievement prize for optical lattice clocks (B025) to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. Several reached it by moving from other opening first choices after reading the colleagues' ballots: Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce. Shared: the two-name attribution, with Katori for the magic-wavelength concept and Jun Ye for record accuracy and stability near 1e-18; independent confirmation across laboratories; and a citation worded around the lattice clock itself. Not shared: how much the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes already cover this ground, how much weight Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Sterr, Gill and Hinkley should carry against the two-name credit, and whether a measurement capability whose largest consequences (redefinition of the second, geodesy, constants) are still prospective counts as a discovery. The citation wordings differ slightly (some add tests of fundamental physics) but are substantively the same.

Danielsson is the only member whose preferred configuration is magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B022) with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, citing a seven-year prediction-to-experiment gap and broad reproduction. He moved to it from his opening first choice, the Event Horizon Telescope (B054), after weighing attribution arguments. Mehlig, who opened with B022 first, has moved to B025. B022 is the first or second alternative of Johansson (second), Lindroth (first), Mehlig (first), Olsson (first) and Pearce (second), but these members do not prefer it now. Shared: the phenomenology is secure and the prediction-plus-experiment structure is attractive. Not shared: whether the unsettled pairing mechanism makes it premature, and whether Bistritzer belongs in the credit (Lindroth's opening proposal omits him).

areas_of_agreement: All eight proposers in the opening named the same two laureates for B025, Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye, and every member ranked B025 in the opening; in round 1 seven of eight prefer it as the sole prize part.
The 1e-18 fractional uncertainty is described as reproduced and intercompared by independent laboratories, so no member raises a doubt about maturity or reproducibility for B025.
Members converge on wording any B025 citation around the magic-wavelength lattice clock and its realisation, not around precision spectroscopy in general.
Several members state that the thorium nuclear clock is not yet mature enough to compete, so Jun Ye's credit would not be split by it at present (Kroll, Olsson, Eriksson, Johansson).
Members broadly accept that the 2025 circuits prize makes circuit QED (B016) hard to scope this year, and that the B016 four-name credit has no agreed three-name cut.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus invention: Danielsson, in his response, questions whether a lattice-clock prize rewards a new phenomenon or an instrument advance. Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce each list this as the strongest reservation against B025 in their own case-against. Kroll cites the Charpak and Hall-Haensch precedents for rewarding measurement inventions. Lindroth argues the clocks feed back into fundamental physics.

Overlap with earlier prizes: the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for ion control and ion clocks sit close to B025, and several members say the committee must state what is distinct about the lattice clock.

How much of the clock's payoff is prospective: the redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and constant-drift or dark-matter searches are described as largely still to come (Danielsson, Lindroth, Pearce).
Whether the committee should prefer B025 or B022: Danielsson frames it as discovery versus capability, while the other seven weigh B022's interpretive immaturity against the clock's maturity.

IceCube (B007) is a new observational window with a firm diffuse flux, but source identification is thin (a single blazar association at about three sigma and Galactic-plane evidence); Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig judge this too immature relative to the clock.
attribution_disputes: B025: Lemonde (SYRTE), Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley, Sterr and Gill contributed to early strontium lattice demonstrations and to the stability record. Members disagree on how much this complicates a two-name credit; Lindroth and Olsson want the citation and deliberation to acknowledge it explicitly, while Johansson and Pearce hold that concept and record performance are each clearly traceable.

B022: Lindroth proposes only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, while Danielsson and Mehlig argue Bistritzer, first author of the 2011 prediction, should not be dropped. Experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero (Cao, Fatemi, and the Dean, Young and Kim groups) cannot be captured by three names.

B054 (Event Horizon Telescope): the Falcke, Doeleman and Zensus split within a collaboration of about 300 is contested, and Danielsson himself now treats attribution as more serious here than for B022.
B007 (IceCube): the Halzen and Spiering pair is contestable against the AMANDA, DUMAND and Baikal lineage and the large collaboration.
B016 (circuit QED): proposers use three different three-name sets drawn from Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf and Girvin.
maturity_disputes: B022: Danielsson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce regard the phenomenology as secure but the pairing mechanism, phase diagram and sample or twist-angle dependence as unsettled after about eight years. Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth say this makes it early for this cycle, but Danielsson and Mehlig do not call it premature.
B007: the diffuse flux is established, while the source astronomy is thin; Lindroth would prefer to wait for the source picture to firm up.

B025: no member raises a maturity concern, although Lindroth notes the second has not yet been redefined, and Olsson and Kroll flag that the 1e-18 figures were recalled and not verified against primary comparisons.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: professional proximity to the circuit QED community through Chalmers, WACQT and collaborations with Per Delsing, C. M. Wilson and Anton Frisk Kockum; he states he should recuse or stand back from any B016 discussion. No tie to Katori or Ye is recorded.

Kroll: research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, part of the lineage of precision laser spectroscopy near the Ye work, with no documented direct collaboration with Katori or Ye; also WACQT management (near B016) and quantum-memory or cold-atom-adjacent work (near B037). Kroll asks the committee to judge recusal.

Olsson: documented institutional connection to Japan through JSPS and University of Tokyo fellowships, where Katori is, to her recollection, based; she suggests a recusal check although no collaboration or co-authorship with Katori or Ye is documented. She also discounts her own first-place B008 as being in her own field.

Pearce (chair): professional ties to the astroparticle community (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur); he discounts his opening enthusiasm for B007 and would consider recusal if B007 were leading. No conflict is apparent for B025.

Eriksson: professional proximity to B029, B036 and B022 through electronic-structure theory and magnetism; no personal or institutional connection to any credited name. Lindroth: knows the atomic-physics community without documented ties to Katori or Ye. Danielsson and Mehlig: no specific conflict apparent.
questions_for_round2: What is the scope statement that distinguishes a lattice-clock prize (B025) from the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for ion control and ion clocks, and should it be framed as an invention that has already produced new physics or as a measurement capability?

Is a two-name credit for Katori and Jun Ye defensible given the claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Sterr, Gill and Hinkley, and if so, how should the citation be worded so it does not overclaim the whole field? Lindroth was asked by Pearce whether Ye's role is better described as an accuracy and many-body programme or as a distinct invention.

Danielsson is the only member preferring B022: should the committee treat the unsettled pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder as disqualifying for this cycle, and if B022 were advanced, should Bistritzer be named alongside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero?

Do the members who disclosed proximity (Olsson to Katori's institution, Kroll to Hall's laboratory, Johansson and Kroll to circuit QED) judge that any of these requires recusal on B025, and can B016 be discussed without Johansson?

If the clock is the leading candidate, would any member change an alternative or preference on the grounds of the discovery-versus-capability criterion, in particular for B007, B054, B036 or B029, and what evidence on IceCube source identification would change the maturity assessment?

Should the 1e-18 uncertainty figures and the chronology of the first lattice clocks be verified against primary intercomparisons before the citation is fixed, as Olsson proposes, since several members relied on recalled values?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a strong shift toward B025: Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce moved from other opening preferences, and Kroll and Lindroth keep it first. Danielsson remains on B022. The remaining open questions concern scope relative to earlier prizes, the discovery-versus-capability criterion, and the margin of credit around Katori and Ye, not scientific reproducibility or maturity. B022 is the most frequently named alternative. This summary records only positions stated in the eight files and takes no view on the outcome.
